subject: Urgent: Dedicated pool autoscaler failure — proposed bridging and next steps
messages:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: aisha.gomez@evergreenretail.com, ops-team@evergreenretail.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Dedicated pool autoscaler failure — proposed bridging and next steps

Hi Aisha / Evergreen ops team,

Thanks for the heads up this morning — I wanted to reach you directly with what we know and an immediate remediation plan. Between 08:58–09:05 PT we observed an autoscaler coordination mismatch in your dedicated GPU pool that prevented warm nodes from being provisioned under a burst. That caused request queuing and increased tail latency for a subset of calls (mainly >1k token generation paths).

Impact summary (initial):
- Time window: ~08:58–09:05 PT
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (large-seq workloads)
- Customer impact: elevated token latency (95th -> 3.2s), transient 429s on burst spikes

Immediate actions we propose (need your go-ahead for the routing change):
1) Route new large-seq requests to a compatible, slightly smaller model variant we have warmed in another pool (temporary variance in cost/latency tradeoff).
2) Force-allocate two warm standby nodes into your reserved pool for the next 6 hours to absorb traffic while autoscaler reconciliation runs.
3) Share a sample of request traces/queue IDs so we can prioritize recovery and correlate errors.

Attachments: incident-snapshot-20270516.txt (small diagnostics dump), evg-queue-sample-20270516.json (anonymized request ids).

If you approve (reply with "approve routing"), we will execute step 1 immediately and schedule the warm-standby allocation within 15 minutes. If you prefer no routing change, we will proceed with forced warm nodes only, but recovery time will lengthen.

Really sorry for the disruption — we want to minimize customer visible impact while we complete the reconciler fix. I’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable.

-Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime
From: aisha.gomez@evergreenretail.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@evergreenretail.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:05:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Dedicated pool autoscaler failure — proposed bridging and next steps

Ben,

Thanks for the quick summary. We are seeing order-processing spikes and downstream queues backing up; the delay is causing some throttles in our inventory pipeline. Two quick questions before we greenlight routing:
1) Estimated recovery if you do NOT change routing and only force the warm nodes?
2) If we route to the smaller model variant, what is the expected change in average latency per request and are there any tokenization/compatibility differences that could change outputs?

Also please preserve logs for billing/credit review — we will expect a formal credit/incident note. We agree you should start with the warm nodes; route only if forced nodes don't bring latency down in the next 30–45 min.

Aisha Gomez
Director, Platform Operations
Evergreen Retail

On Sun, May 16, 2027 at 09:12 AM ben_carter@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Aisha / Evergreen ops team,
> 
> Thanks for the heads up this morning — I wanted to reach you directly with what we know and an immediate remediation plan....
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: aisha.gomez@evergreenretail.com, ops-team@evergreenretail.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:30:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Dedicated pool autoscaler failure — proposed bridging and next steps

Aisha — appreciate the clarity and the ask to preserve logs. Quick answers and actions taken: 

Answers:
- If we only force warm nodes (no routing) we expect latency to drop to near-normal within ~20–35 minutes for steady traffic, but you may still see intermittent 429s during high microbursts while the allocator stabilizes.
- Routing to the compatible variant reduces average latency by ~0.4–1.1s on these sequences for the warm nodes we prepared; output quality is functionally equivalent for the vast majority of prompts we tested — there are minor response length differences in ~3% of sampled prompts. We’ve validated tokenization compatibility.

Actions (completed):
- Force-allocated two warm standby nodes into Evergreen's reserved pool at 11:05 PT.
- Triggered a manual allocator reconciliation; logs are being aggregated (attached).
- Holding routing change until you confirm; if you prefer a staged canary we can route 10% of traffic first.

Commitment: If this event meets our SLA thresholds for credit, we will issue a four-hour usage credit against the impacted window (subject to standard terms). We will follow with a formal incident bulletin and a postmortem within 72 hours.

Link to runbook and notes: https://drive.redwood.company/ops/runbooks/autoscaler-fallback-v2
Attachments: incident-snapshot-20270516.txt (diagnostics).

Please let me know if you want us to start a 10% canary now; otherwise we’ll keep the forced nodes in place and continue monitoring.

-Ben
On behalf of Redwood Inference Ops
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha.gomez@evergreenretail.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: post-incident coordination and requested artifacts

Hi Aisha / Ben / Marissa,

Thanks for the coordination yesterday. Per our internal review and the timeline Ben shared, we want to propose the following next steps to close out and prevent recurrence:

1) Postmortem call (60m) — propose Tue 2027-05-18 10:00 PT. Agenda: timeline review, root cause hypothesis, mitigations (allocator watchdogs, canary warm-up change), customer impact reconciliation, and credits.
2) Artifact request from Evergreen: a) a small set of anonymized request traces for the 08:50–09:20 window (we already have evg-queue-sample-20270516.json but if you can include a few end-to-end trace ids we can correlate); b) any downstream queue logs that show retries.
3) Our proposed compensatory path: 4 hours of usage credit (applied to the billing account for the impacted routes) + a technical review of your workload with our Optimize team to reduce hot-path risk.

We will prepare a short postmortem draft and circulate it before the call; please tell us if you want an external-facing customer-ready version versus a joint technical postmortem.

If Tue 10:00 PT doesn't work, propose two alternative times and we will align.

-Karthik Iyer
Senior Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
